mainTopic: Holding back excess joy, and the proper mindset, timing, direction and manner of תפילה
overview: This amud opens with stories of חכמים who felt the joy at a wedding had gone too far. מר בריה דרבינא and רב אשי each broke an expensive cup. רב המנונא זוטי sang about death and asked where our תורה and מצוות are to protect us. רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, rules that one may not fill his mouth with laughter in this world, and ריש לקיש lived by this all his life. The גמרא then turns to the right frame of mind for תפילה. It says to begin from a הלכה פסוקה, a settled ruling, or from שמחה של מצוה, and to part from a friend with a דבר הלכה, which it illustrates with a story about רב כהנא and רב שימי בר אשי. Next come the laws of how to pray: focus the heart, as רבי עקיבא did, and do not burden the ציבור. From דניאל, דוד, חנה and שלמה we learn to pray three set times a day, facing ירושלים, quietly, and with praise before requests. Finally, רב המנונא draws four הלכות from חנה's prayer, and רבי אלעזר begins a lesson from עלי's rebuke that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The expensive cup is broken and the guests grow serious
steps.stepSummary: The end of the story of מר בריה דרבינא: he breaks a cup worth 400 זוז in front of the overly joyful חכמים, and they become sad.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought a precious cup worth four hundred זוז, broke it in front of them, and they became sad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began just before: at his son's wedding, מר בריה דרבינא saw the חכמים getting too wild with joy. He broke a very expensive cup to make them more serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking something that costs a lot is a shock. It makes people stop and calm down. The goal was not to ruin the wedding but to bring the joy back to a proper level.

phrases.english: He brought a precious cup
phrases.notes: "He" is מר בריה דרבינא, from the story right before this, at his son's wedding.

phrases.english: worth four hundred zuz,
and broke it in front of them, and they became sad.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּיתִי כָּסָא דְמוֹקְרָא בַּת אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story of מר בריה דרבינא's wedding that began earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When joy goes too far, it is proper to do something that makes people more serious.

steps.title: רב אשי breaks a white glass cup at his son's wedding
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sees the חכמים rejoicing too much at his son's wedding and breaks a valuable white glass cup in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי made a wedding feast for his son. He saw the חכמים rejoicing very much. He brought a cup of white glass, broke it in front of them, and they became sad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story just like the first one, this time about רב אשי. He also breaks a costly cup to calm down the overly joyful guests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate great חכמים did the same thing. This shows it was an accepted practice, not one person's odd idea. White glass was very valuable at that time, so the loss got people's attention.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi made a wedding feast for his son,
he saw the Sages
who were rejoicing very much.
He brought a cup of white glass,
and broke it in front of them, and they became sad.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי עֲבַד הִילּוּלָא לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that repeats the same action as step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי also broke a costly cup to hold back too much joy.

steps.title: רב המנונא זוטי sings a song about death
steps.stepSummary: At the wedding of מר בריה דרבינא, the חכמים ask רב המנונא זוטי to sing, and he sings "Woe to us, for we will die."
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to רב המנונא זוטי at the wedding feast of מר בריה דרבינא: Let the master sing for us. He said to them: Woe to us, for we will die! Woe to us, for we will die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a third story. Instead of breaking a cup, רב המנונא זוטי uses a song to make the joyful crowd remember that life is short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is the same as breaking the cup: to calm down joy that has gone too far. The method is different. Here the reminder comes through words, by thinking about death, instead of through a shocking loss of money.

keyTerms.meaning: let the master sing for us

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא זוּטֵי
phrases.english: The Sages said to Rav Hamnuna Zuti
at the wedding feast of Mar son of Ravina:
Let the master sing for us.
He said to them: Woe to us, for we will die!
Woe to us, for we will die!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא זוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third story with the same goal, but it uses a song instead of breaking a cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remembering death is another way to keep wedding joy in check.

steps.title: The guests ask what the chorus should be
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב המנונא זוטי what line they should sing back to him as a response.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What should we answer after you?
steps.whatsHappening: The guests ask for the chorus, the response line they should sing back. This question sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a celebration, the crowd usually sings a response after the leader. Their question gives רב המנונא זוטי the chance to add a second, deeper message to his song.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אֲנַן מָה נַעֲנֵי בָּתְרָךְ?
phrases.english: They said to him: What should we answer after you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אֲנַן מָה נַעֲנֵי בָּתְרָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the song from step 3 by asking for its chorus.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What response line should the guests sing?

steps.title: The chorus: where are the תורה and מצוות that protect us?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא זוטי gives the chorus: "Where is the תורה and where is the מצוה that will protect us?"
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Where is the תורה, and where is the מצוה, that will protect us?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא זוטי answers with the chorus. It asks whether we have enough תורה and מצוות to protect us when we die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line reminded the guests that everyone dies. The chorus adds what really matters after death: our תורה and מצוות. Together the two lines turn the guests' joy into serious thinking.
steps.whatToRemember: Three stories, one lesson: when wedding joy goes too far, the חכמים brought people back to seriousness, either by breaking a costly cup or by reminding them of death and of the תורה and מצוות that protect us.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הֵי תּוֹרָה, וְהֵי מִצְוָה
phrases.english: He said to them: Where is the Torah, and where is the מצוה
that will protect us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הֵי תּוֹרָה, וְהֵי מִצְוָה דְּמַגְּנוּ עֲלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The chorus is: Where is the תורה and where is the מצוה that will protect us?

steps.title: No filling one's mouth with laughter in this world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, rules that a person may not fill his mouth with laughter in this world. He learns it from a פסוק in תהלים: "then" our mouths will fill with laughter, meaning only when the nations see ה׳'s great acts for us.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: It is forbidden for a person to fill his mouth with laughter in this world, as it says: "Then our mouth will be filled with laughter and our tongue with song." When will that be? At the time when "they will say among the nations: ה׳ has done great things with these."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a general rule that explains the stories above: complete, mouth-filling laughter is not allowed in this world. רבי יוחנן proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the word "then" (אז). It shows that full laughter belongs to a future time, the time of the גאולה, when the nations will see ה׳'s great acts. Until that time arrives, our joy must always hold something back.

keyTerms.meaning: to fill his mouth with laughter, meaning complete, unlimited laughter
this world, the present time before the גאולה
then, only at that future time

steps.confusionAlert: The rule does not ban all joy or smiling. It bans filling one's mouth with laughter, meaning total, unlimited laughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the source behind the practice of holding back some of our joy, even at happy times, while we are still waiting for the גאולה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is forbidden for a person to fill his mouth with laughter
in this world,
as it says: "Then our mouth will be filled with laughter
and our tongue with song."
When? At the time when "they will say among the nations:
ה׳ has done great things with these."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general rule and its source from a פסוק, which explains the stories about holding back joy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may not fill his mouth with laughter in this world. Full laughter is kept for the time of the גאולה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש never laughed fully again
steps.stepSummary: From the time ריש לקיש heard this teaching from his teacher רבי יוחנן, he never filled his mouth with laughter for the rest of his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about ריש לקיש that all his days he did not fill his mouth with laughter in this world, from the time he heard it from רבי יוחנן his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how seriously this rule was taken: ריש לקיש kept it for the rest of his life once he learned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows that the rule in step 6 was not just an idea. A great אמורא lived by it every day. It also shows how ריש לקיש accepted his teacher's words completely.

keyTerms.meaning: they said about him (a phrase that introduces a story about someone's behavior)
all his days, his whole life

steps.whatToRemember: The stories and the rule teach one lesson: in this world, before the גאולה, even our happiest moments should keep some seriousness. ריש לקיש lived this way his whole life.

phrases.english: They said about Reish Lakish
that all his days he did not fill his mouth with laughter
in this world,
from the time he heard it from Rabbi Yochanan his teacher.
phrases.notes: "It" is the rule from the step before: no filling your mouth with laughter in this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule of step 6 being kept in practice by ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש kept the rule against full laughter for his whole life after hearing it from רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Do not go straight from a court case or open debate into prayer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one should not begin תפילה straight out of judging a דין or debating a הלכה. One should begin it out of a הלכה פסוקה, a settled ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: You should not stand up to pray straight out of judging a case, and not straight out of working through an open question of הלכה. Instead, pray straight out of learning a הלכה that is already decided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us what to be busy with right before we start praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court case or an unsettled הלכה keeps your mind working and worrying, so it would pull your thoughts away during תפילה. A הלכה פסוקה is finished and clear, so your mind is calm and free to focus. The point is to enter תפילה from Torah learning, but from a kind that will not distract you.

keyTerms.meaning: A court case or legal judgment
A הלכה question that is still being worked out
A settled, decided ruling with nothing left to argue about

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying to avoid Torah learning before תפילה. It says to learn something settled, so your mind is not stuck on an open question while you pray.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One does not stand up to pray
not straight out of judging a case,
and not straight out of a matter of הלכה,
phrases.notes: He means a הלכה question you are still thinking through and haven't settled yet.

phrases.english: but rather straight out of a decided הלכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's topic, the proper mindset before תפילה, after the stories about not filling one's mouth with laughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not start תפילה straight from a דין or an open הלכה question. Start it from a הלכה פסוקה.

steps.title: What counts as a decided ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete example of a הלכה פסוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is an example of a decided הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an example so we know what a הלכה פסוקה looks like in real life. This sets up the answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the term הלכה פסוקה without defining it. The גמרא wants a clear model case of a ruling so settled that it will not distract a person.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is it like?": a request for a concrete example or case

phrases.english: And what is an example of a decided הלכה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the key term in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of a הלכה פסוקה.

steps.title: אביי's example: the women's stringency of seven clean days
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with the teaching of רבי זירא: בנות ישראל took on themselves to count seven clean days even for a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Like this teaching of רבי זירא. רבי זירא said: בנות ישראל were strict on themselves. Even if they see a drop of blood as small as a mustard seed, they count seven clean days for it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first example of a הלכה פסוקה: the accepted practice that women count seven clean days for even a tiny drop of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This practice is accepted by everyone and no one argues about it, so it is fully settled. Since there is nothing to debate, learning it right before תפילה will not keep the mind busy.

keyTerms.meaning: They were strict on themselves and took on an extra stringency
A mustard seed, used here as a measure for something very small
Seven clean days counted before becoming טהורה

phrases.english: אביי said:
Like this teaching of רבי זירא,
for רבי זירא said:
Jewish women were strict on themselves,
so that even if they see a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed,
they sit seven clean days for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with a first example.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הלכה פסוקה is like רבי זירא's teaching that women count seven clean days for even a mustard-seed-sized drop of blood.

steps.title: רבא's example: bringing grain in its chaff to avoid מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different example, from רב הושעיא: a person may bring his grain in while it is still in its chaff, so his animal can eat it, and it is פטור from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Like this teaching of רב הושעיא. רב הושעיא said: A person may use a clever, permitted trick with his grain. He brings it in while it is still in its chaff so that his animal can eat from it, and it is פטור from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, different example of a הלכה פסוקה: the permitted trick of bringing in grain still in its chaff so it stays פטור from מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like אביי, רבא picks a ruling that is clear and accepted, with no open argument. He simply chooses a case from the laws of מעשר instead of the laws of טהרה. Both examples teach the same idea: a settled ruling that will not distract a person during תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Uses a clever trick, a legal way to arrange things so an obligation does not apply
Chaff, the husk around the grain
Tithes, the portion of produce that must be separated and given away

steps.whatToRemember: Before תפילה, learn something settled, a הלכה פסוקה, not an open debate. אביי's example comes from women's seven clean days, and רבא's example comes from bringing grain in its chaff to avoid מעשר.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Like this teaching of רב הושעיא,
for רב הושעיא said:
A person may use a clever trick with his grain
and bring it in while it is still in its chaff,
so that his animal can eat from it,
and it is exempt from tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different example answering the same question that אביי answered in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הלכה פסוקה is like רב הושעיא's teaching that one may bring grain in its chaff for animal feed and stay פטור from מעשר.

steps.title: A third example of a settled ruling: blood taken from a consecrated animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another example of a הלכה פסוקה: רב הונא in the name of רבי זעירא rules that blood let from a בהמת קדשים is forbidden for benefit, and one who uses it commits מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, use a ruling like רב הונא's. רב הונא said in the name of רבי זעירא: if someone lets blood from an animal set aside as a קרבן, the blood may not be used for any benefit, and someone who uses it is guilty of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still answering the question from Step 9, "what is a הלכה פסוקה?" It gives a third possible example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example is a short, clear, finished ruling with no open debate. Here the ruling is that the blood counts as holy property. Benefit from it is forbidden, and using it is real מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you wish, say": introduces another option or answer
One who lets blood (draws blood from an animal)
An animal set aside as a קרבן
Forbidden to get any benefit from it

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
like this ruling of רב הונא,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא:
phrases.english: for רב הונא said that רבי זעירא said:
one who lets blood from a consecrated animal,
it is forbidden to benefit from it,
and one commits מעילה with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, alongside אביי's and רבא's examples, to the question of what counts as a הלכה פסוקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is a concrete example of a הלכה פסוקה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי זעירא's ruling: blood let from a בהמת קדשים is forbidden for benefit, and one who uses it commits מעילה.

steps.title: How the חכמים and רב אשי actually prepared for prayer
steps.stepSummary: In practice, the חכמים followed our משנה, while רב אשי followed the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים acted according to our משנה. רב אשי acted according to the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how people actually practiced. There were two sources about how to start תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says to begin תפילה with a serious mind. The ברייתא (Step 8) says to begin from a הלכה פסוקה. The חכמים prepared the משנה's way, and רב אשי prepared the ברייתא's way, so both approaches were in real use.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two good ways to come into תפילה: with a serious mind (the משנה), or straight after a settled ruling (the ברייתא). Both were practiced.

phrases.english: The Sages acted according to our Mishnah,
phrases.notes: Our משנה said to stand for תפילה only with a serious, heavy-headed mood.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi acted according to the baraita.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא from Step 8: start תפילה from a settled ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן עָבְדִי כְּמַתְנִיתִין, רַב אָשֵׁי עָבֵיד כְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of how to come into תפילה by reporting actual practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both approaches were practiced: the חכמים began תפילה with seriousness, as in the משנה, and רב אשי began it after a הלכה פסוקה, as in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The right mood for starting prayer: the joy of a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists moods one should not start תפילה from: sadness, laziness, laughter, chatter, lightheadedness and idle talk. One should start from שמחה של מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: do not stand up to pray straight out of sadness, laziness, laughter, chatting, lightheadedness or empty talk. Stand up to pray out of the joy of doing a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the right state of mind for starting תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of moods are ruled out: heavy ones (sadness, laziness) and light ones (laughter, chatter, lightheadedness, idle talk). The right mood sits in between: real joy, but joy that comes from a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The joy that comes from doing a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Joy is not the problem here. Laughter and lightheadedness are ruled out, but שמחה של מצוה is exactly what is wanted. The question is where the joy comes from.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One does not stand to pray
not out of sadness,
nor out of laziness,
nor out of laughter,
nor out of chatter,
nor out of lightheadedness,
nor out of idle matters,
but rather out of the joy of a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עוֹמְדִין לְהִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the same theme of how to come into תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Begin תפילה neither from heavy moods nor from light ones, but from שמחה של מצוה.

steps.title: How to part from a friend: with a word of הלכה
steps.stepSummary: Using the same pattern, the ברייתא teaches that one should not take leave of a friend in the middle of chatter, laughter, lightheadedness or idle talk, but with a דבר הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way, a person should not leave his friend in the middle of chatting, laughing, lightheadedness or empty talk. He should leave him with a word of הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא carries its rule over to a new situation: saying goodbye to a friend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן ("and likewise") tells us the same idea applies here. This list is shorter: sadness and laziness are not mentioned. The right way to part is with a דבר הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise: applies the same idea to a new case
Take leave of, part from, his friend
A word or matter of הלכה

phrases.english: And likewise, a person should not take leave of his friend
not out of chatter,
nor out of laughter,
nor out of lightheadedness,
nor out of idle matters,
but rather out of a matter of halacha.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן לֹא יִפָּטֵר אָדָם מֵחֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא applies its pattern to parting from a friend.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should part from a friend with a דבר הלכה, not with light or empty talk.

steps.title: Support from the early prophets, who ended with praise and comfort
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports its rule from the early נביאים, who ended their words with praise and comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see this from the early נביאים: they ended their words with words of praise and comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a source for the rule about parting well. The early נביאים always finished on a good, meaningful note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a pattern, not a single פסוק. The נביאים made sure their last words were praise and comfort. In the same way, a person should make the end of a meeting meaningful, with a דבר הלכה rather than empty talk.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we have found: introduces supporting evidence

steps.whatToRemember: How you start matters (begin תפילה with שמחה של מצוה), and how you end matters (part from a friend with a דבר הלכה, just as the נביאים ended with praise and comfort).

phrases.english: For so we have found with the early prophets,
that they concluded their words
with words of praise and consolation.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בַּנְּבִיאִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for Step 15's rule about how to part from a friend.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should part from a friend with a meaningful word, a דבר הלכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The pattern of the early נביאים, who ended their words with praise and comfort.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: part from a friend with a דבר הלכה
steps.stepSummary: מרי, the grandson of רב הונא, teaches a ברייתא with the same rule as before: part from a friend only with a דבר הלכה. He adds the reason: this way your friend will remember you.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the same way, מרי (the grandson of רב הונא, who was the son of רבי ירמיה בר אבא) taught: A person should only take leave of his friend with a matter of הלכה, because that way the friend will remember him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that backs up the rule from step 15 and adds a reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 already said to part with a דבר הלכה. This ברייתא, introduced with 'וכן' ('and so'), supports that rule. It also gives a new reason: the Torah idea you share makes your friend remember you.

keyTerms.meaning: And so taught: brings another source that says the same thing

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תְּנָא מָרִי בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: And so taught מרי, the grandson of רב הונא,
son of רבי ירמיה בר אבא:
phrases.notes: This is one long family line: מרי is the grandson of רב הונא, and רב הונא is the son of רבי ירמיה בר אבא.

phrases.english: A person should not take leave of his friend
except in the middle of a matter of הלכה,
because through this he will remember him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תְּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא that agrees with step 15's rule and gives a reason for it.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should part from a friend with a דבר הלכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא taught by מרי, grandson of רב הונא

steps.title: רב כהנא walks רב שימי and asks about the palm trees
steps.stepSummary: As an example of parting with Torah, רב כהנא walks רב שימי בר אשי to the palm groves of בבל. When they get there, he asks whether a popular saying is true: that these palm trees go back to אדם הראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רב כהנא, who walked with רב שימי בר אשי from פום נהרא to the palm groves of בבל. When they got there, he said to him: Master, is it true what people say, that these palm trees of בבל have been here from the time of אדם הראשון until now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the rule in action. רב כהנא asks a question as they are about to part, and this sets up the Torah teaching that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כי הא' ('like this one') tell us the story is an example of parting with a דבר הלכה. The question about the palm trees opens the door for רב שימי to share a teaching at the moment of parting.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this: brings an example story
Accompanied him, walked him on his way

phrases.english: Like this story of רב כהנא,
who walked רב שימי בר אשי on his way

phrases.aramaic: מִפּוּם נַהֲרָא עַד בֵּי צִנְיָתָא דְּבָבֶל.
phrases.english: from פום נהרא to the palm grove of בבל.
When he got there,
he (רב כהנא) said to him: Master,
is it really true, what people say:
these palm trees of בבל
have been here from אדם הראשון until now?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא אַלְוְיֵיהּ לְרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the rule from step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the popular saying true that the palm trees of בבל go back to אדם הראשון?

steps.title: A puzzling פסוק: how can people settle where no one passed?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי says the question reminds him of a teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. That teaching starts with a puzzle in a פסוק: if no one ever passed through the land, why say no one settled there?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You reminded me of a teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. For רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: What is meant by the פסוק 'In a land through which no man passed and where no person settled'? Since no one even passed through, how could anyone have settled there?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי starts his answer by quoting a teaching that first points out a problem in a פסוק. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nobody ever passed through a land, obviously nobody lived there. So the second half of the פסוק, 'no person settled there,' seems extra. This extra phrase is the hook for the explanation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written: opens an explanation of a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The puzzle is not a question on רב כהנא. It is a difficulty inside the פסוק that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא is about to solve, and his solution answers רב כהנא.

phrases.english: He (רב שימי) said to him:
You reminded me of a teaching
of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא,
for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said:
What is meant by what is written:
"In a land through which no man passed
and where no person settled"?
But since no one even passed through,
how could anyone have settled there?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּלֹא עָבַר הֵיאַךְ יָשַׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב שימי begins answering רב כהנא by bringing a teaching that opens with a difficulty in a פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no one passed through, then no one settled there either, so 'no person settled' seems to add nothing.

steps.title: אדם הראשון decided which lands would be settled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that 'אדם' in the פסוק means אדם הראשון. Any land he decided should be settled became settled, and any land he did not decide on stayed empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק comes to tell you: every land that אדם הראשון decreed should be settled was settled, and every land that אדם הראשון did not decree should be settled was not settled.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching solves the puzzle of the פסוק, and this also answers רב כהנא's question about the palm trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אדם' is read as אדם הראשון, so the phrase is no longer extra: it means a land אדם הראשון never decided to settle. So the saying about the palm trees makes sense: since אדם הראשון's time, this land was meant for palm trees. רב כהנא and רב שימי בר אשי parted with a new Torah idea, just as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to tell you: introduces the real meaning
For settlement, to be lived in

steps.whatToRemember: Parting with Torah works: רב כהנא's simple question at the moment of parting led to a new teaching, so the two would remember each other through it.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶרֶץ שֶׁגָּזַר עָלֶיהָ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לְיִשּׁוּב
phrases.english: every land that אדם הראשון decreed should be settled
phrases.notes: The word 'אדם' in the פסוק is being read as אדם הראשון.

phrases.english: was settled.
And every land that he did not decree
(that is, אדם הראשון) should be settled
was not settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the difficulty in the פסוק from step 19, and so answers רב כהנא's question from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the פסוק ('אדם' means אדם הראשון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No person settled' seems to repeat 'no man passed through.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase teaches that only lands אדם הראשון decided to settle became settled, which supports the saying about the palm trees of בבל.

steps.title: רב מרדכי walks רב שימי a long way
steps.stepSummary: Another story: רב מרדכי walked his teacher רב שימי בר אשי from הגרוניא to בי כיפי. Some say it was all the way to בי דורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי walked רב שימי בר אשי on his way from הגרוניא to בי כיפי. And some say: until בי דורא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short story about another student who walked רב שימי בר אשי a long distance when he left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of walking someone on his way when parting. It shows how much honor a student gave his teacher. 'ואמרי לה' brings a second version of how far he went.

phrases.aramaic: רַב מָרְדְּכַי אַלְוְיֵיהּ לְרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: רב מרדכי walked רב שימי בר אשי on his way
from הגרוניא until בי כיפי.
And some say: until בי דורא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרְדְּכַי אַלְוְיֵיהּ לְרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the story of רב כהנא with another story of a student walking רב שימי בר אשי on his way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב מרדכי honored his teacher by walking him a great distance, from הגרוניא to בי כיפי, or according to some, to בי דורא.

steps.title: One who prays must aim his heart toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a person who is davening must direct his heart to שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person who prays must aim his heart toward Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of getting ready for תפילה and quotes a ברייתא: when you daven, your heart must be aimed at שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a basic rule about כוונה, the inner focus of תפילה. It is not enough to say the words; the heart has to be pointed toward הקב"ה. The next step brings a hint from a פסוק for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: That he should aim/focus his heart

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who prays must
focus his heart toward Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about walking a teacher and returns to the main topic of preparing for תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who prays must direct his heart toward שמים.

steps.title: אבא שאול's hint from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול brings a פסוק as a sign for the rule: when the heart is prepared, ה׳'s ear listens.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: There is a sign for this: 'Prepare their heart, Your ear will listen.'
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול backs up the rule about focusing the heart with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects two things: a prepared heart and ה׳ listening. So the hint is that when a person focuses his heart, his תפילה is heard. He calls it a סימן, a sign or hint, not a full proof.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
A sign for the matter:
"Prepare their heart, Your ear will listen."

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule of step 22 with a hint from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That one must focus his heart in תפילה.

steps.title: How רבי עקיבא prayed with the group and alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that רבי עקיבא davened short with the ציבור, but alone he davened so long that he ended up in a different corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said: This was the way of רבי עקיבא. When he prayed with the congregation, he would shorten his prayer and finish, so as not to burden the congregation. But when he prayed by himself, a person would leave him in one corner and find him later in another corner.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells us how רבי עקיבא davened: short with others, very long when alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ציבור he cut his תפילה short because making everyone wait is a burden on them (טורח צבור). Alone, nobody was waiting, so he prayed at length. The detail about moving corners sets up the next question: why did he move so much?

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: This was the custom of Rabbi Akiva:
when he would pray with the congregation,
he would shorten and go up,
phrases.notes: Meaning he would finish quickly and be done.

phrases.english: because of the burden on the congregation.
But when he would pray by himself,
a person would leave him in this corner,
and find him in another corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a living example of כוונה in תפילה, and adds the consideration of not burdening the ציבור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the ציבור, shorten your תפילה to avoid burdening them; alone, one may pray at length.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even a great person's long, focused תפילה must give way to the needs of the ציבור.

steps.title: Why did he move so much?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why רבי עקיבא ended up moving from corner to corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all of this?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops to ask a short question about the story: why would he end up in a different corner? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing in one place is normal during תפילה, so moving across the room is surprising. The question asks what caused it.

phrases.english: And why all of this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the strange detail in step 24 (moving from corner to corner).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made רבי עקיבא move from one corner to another while praying.

steps.title: Because of his bows
steps.stepSummary: The answer: his many bows and prostrations moved him across the room.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of his bowings and prostrations.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: he bowed and bowed down so many times that he slowly moved to another corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He didn't walk on purpose; all the bowing during his long, heartfelt תפילה shifted his place. This shows how deep his כוונה was.

phrases.english: Because of bowings and prostrations.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי כְּרִיעוֹת וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His many bows and prostrations moved him from corner to corner.

steps.title: Pray in a room with windows
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא teaches that one should pray in a house with windows, learned from דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: A person should always pray in a house that has windows, as it says about דניאל: 'And windows were open for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new law about where to daven: in a room with windows. The source is the פסוק about דניאל praying by open windows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא learns practical laws of תפילה from how דניאל prayed. Since the פסוק mentions his open windows, we learn it is proper to pray in a room with windows.

keyTerms.meaning: And windows were open for him (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said:
A person should always pray
in a house that has windows,
as it says: "And windows were open for him, etc."
phrases.notes: דניאל 6:11, where דניאל prays by windows open toward ירושלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם יִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם בְּבַיִת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חַלּוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of laws learned from דניאל's תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should always pray in a room that has windows.

steps.title: תפילה has set times, not all day
steps.stepSummary: One might think a person can pray all day long, but דניאל shows that תפילה is three set times a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person may pray the whole day. But it was already made clear by דניאל: 'And three times a day...'
steps.whatsHappening: Another law from דניאל: תפילה has fixed times. The text first raises a possible thought (pray all day) and then rejects it from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup 'יכול' means 'you might have thought.' The thought is that one can keep praying the whole day. The פסוק says דניאל prayed three times a day, so תפילה is set at fixed times.
steps.whatToRemember: From here: focus your heart in תפילה; don't burden the ציבור; pray in a room with windows; and pray at fixed times, three times a day, like דניאל.
steps.confusionAlert: 'יכול' is not the conclusion. It is a thought the text raises only to reject it.

phrases.english: You might think a person may pray
the entire day;
it was already made clear through Daniel:
"And three times, etc."
phrases.notes: דניאל 6:11: three times a day he knelt and prayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Learns a second law from the same פסוק about דניאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילה is at fixed times, three times a day, not all day long.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source that the daily תפילות are set times, three times a day.

steps.title: Praying three times a day did not start in exile
steps.stepSummary: One might think דניאל only began praying three times a day once he came to בבל. The פסוק says he was doing what he had always done before.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think this practice only began when he came to the exile. The פסוק already says: 'As he had done before this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another wrong idea about דניאל's תפילה and corrects it with words from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could think the three daily תפילות were a new practice that began because of the hard life in גלות. The words 'as he had done before' show this was already his steady habit. So it is a lasting rule and not a reaction to exile.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a wrong idea that the פסוק will correct)

phrases.english: One might think that from when he came to the exile it was begun —
it has already been stated:
"As he had been doing before this."
phrases.notes: דניאל 6:11. This is the same פסוק about דניאל's windows and his three daily תפילות.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל מִשֶּׁבָּא לַגּוֹלָה הוּחַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail learned from the same פסוק about דניאל used in steps 27-28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three daily תפילות were a steady practice from before the exile, not something new because of גלות.

steps.title: We face ירושלים when we pray
steps.stepSummary: One might think a person can face any direction when praying. The פסוק says דניאל prayed facing ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think a person may pray toward any direction he wants. The פסוק teaches: 'facing ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks which direction to face during תפילה and answers from דניאל's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a source, you might think direction does not matter. The פסוק tells us דניאל's windows were open 'facing ירושלים.' That sets the direction for תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us (introduces the proof)
Direction (here; it can also mean wind or spirit)

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם לְכׇל רוּחַ שֶׁיִּרְצֶה —
phrases.english: One might think a person may pray toward any direction he wishes —
the verse teaches: "Facing ירושלים."
phrases.notes: Some versions have לָקֳבֵל, the word in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is נֶגֶד. Both mean 'facing.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם לְכׇל רוּחַ שֶׁיִּרְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Learns a new rule, the direction of תפילה, from the same פסוק about דניאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should face ירושלים when praying.

steps.title: The three תפילות are spread out over the day
steps.stepSummary: One might think all three תפילות could be said together at one time. דוד already made clear they are said at evening, morning and noon.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he can include all three at one time. דוד already made it clear, as it is written: 'Evening, and morning, and noon...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the three תפילות can be said back to back. It answers with a פסוק from דוד in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דניאל's פסוק tells us there are three תפילות, but it does not say when to say them. So the ברייתא brings a different source. דוד lists three separate times of day, which shows each תפילה has its own time.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the switch in sources. The first rules came from דניאל, but this one comes from דוד, because דניאל's פסוק does not say when in the day to pray.

phrases.english: One might think he may include them all at one time —
it was already made clear by David,
as it is written: "Evening and morning and noon, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהֵא כּוֹלְלָן בְּבַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 28, which taught there are three תפילות, and now teaches that they are spread over the day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three daily תפילות must be said at separate times: evening, morning and noon.

steps.title: The עמידה is said quietly
steps.stepSummary: One might think a person should say his תפילה out loud. חנה already showed that her voice was not heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he should make his voice heard in his תפילה. חנה already made it clear, as it says: 'and her voice was not heard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list by asking whether we pray out loud. It answers from the story of חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that you should pray loudly is corrected by חנה's example. Her lips moved, but her voice could not be heard. This is the source for saying the עמידה quietly.

keyTerms.meaning: Make his voice heard out loud
חנה, the mother of שמואל, whose תפילה is a model for us

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא teaches the basics of תפילה, one 'one might think' at a time. There are three set times a day, and this was a lasting practice from before the exile. We face ירושלים. The three are spread out across the day (דוד). The עמידה is said quietly (חנה).
steps.whyThisMatters: חנה's תפילה becomes a main source for many הלכות of the עמידה. This step opens that topic.

phrases.english: One might think he should make his voice heard in his prayer —
it was already made clear by Hannah,
as it is stated: "And her voice could not be heard."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יַשְׁמִיעַ קוֹלוֹ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more rule to the list, this time learned from a third source, חנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not make his voice heard during the עמידה.

steps.title: Praise comes before requests, learned from שלמה
steps.stepSummary: One might think a person should first ask for his needs and only then praise. שלמה's prayer shows that רנה (praise) comes first and then תפילה (requests).
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think a person should ask for his needs first and pray afterward. שלמה already made it clear, as it says: 'To hear the song and the prayer.' 'Song' means praise, and 'prayer' means request.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא adds one more lesson to its list of 'One might think…' teachings. This one is about the order of the prayer: praise first, then requests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists רנה before תפילה. The גמרא reads רנה as praise and תפילה as personal requests. Since praise is listed first, a person should praise ה׳ before he asks for his own needs.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a wrong idea that the פסוק then corrects)
Song; here it means praise of ה׳
A request; asking for what one needs

phrases.english: One might think a person should ask for his needs
and afterward pray
It was already made clear by שלמה
as it says: "To hear the song and the prayer"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:28, from שלמה's prayer when he dedicated the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: "Song" is prayer of praise
"Prayer" is request

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִשְׁאַל אָדָם צְרָכָיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of 'One might think…' lessons learned from figures in תנ״ך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In תפילה, praise of ה׳ comes before personal requests.

steps.title: No requests right after אמת ויציב, but anything after the עמידה
steps.stepSummary: Because praise must come first, one does not add requests after אמת ויציב, right before the עמידה. After the עמידה, though, one may add even something as long as the יום כיפור confession.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not say any request after 'אמת ויציב'. But after the תפילה, he may say even something as long as the order of the confession of יום כיפור.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical rule from the last step. It says where requests may not go and where they may go freely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after אמת ויציב, a person is about to start the עמידה, which opens with praise. So he must not jump to requests there. Once the עמידה is done, the order 'praise then request' has already been kept, so there is no limit on extra requests.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה after קריאת שמע in the morning, said right before the עמידה
יום כיפור, the Day of Atonement

phrases.english: One does not say a matter of request
after "אמת ויציב"
But after the תפילה

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כְּסֵדֶר וִדּוּי שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: even something like the order of the confession of יום כיפור, he may say

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין אוֹמֵר דְּבַר בַּקָּשָׁה אַחַר ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'praise before requests' rule from step 33 to the actual order of the prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No requests between אמת ויציב and the עמידה; after the עמידה, unlimited personal requests are allowed.

steps.title: רב also allows long personal prayers after the עמידה
steps.stepSummary: רב is quoted saying the same thing. Personal needs can be asked in שומע תפילה, and after the עמידה one may add even something as long as the יום כיפור confession.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: Even though they said a person may ask for his needs in 'שומע תפילה', if he wants to say them after his prayer, he may say even something as long as the order of יום כיפור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא's statement that supports what was just taught. The words 'איתמר נמי' tell us this is backing for the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב adds one detail: inside the עמידה, the place for personal requests is the ברכה of שומע תפילה. But that does not limit him. After the עמידה he may add as much as he wants, just like step 34 said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (an אמורא said the same thing)
The ברכה in the עמידה ending 'Who hears prayer', where personal requests may be added

phrases.english: It was also stated

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
phrases.english: רב חייא בר אשי said that רב said
Even though they said
a person asks for his needs in "שומע תפילה"
if he comes to say them after his prayer

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כְּסֵדֶר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: even like the order of יום כיפור, he may say it

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 34 with a matching statement from רב.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that unlimited personal requests may be added after the עמידה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב, quoted by רב חייא בר אשי.
steps.whatToRemember: Praise comes first. Inside the עמידה, personal requests go in שומע תפילה. After the עמידה, you may add as much as you like.

steps.title: Four הלכות of תפילה learned from חנה
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא learns from the פסוקים about חנה: one must focus his heart, say the words with his lips, not raise his voice, and a drunk person may not pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: How many great הלכות can be learned from these פסוקים of חנה! 'And חנה spoke in her heart' — from here, one who prays must focus his heart. 'Only her lips moved' — from here, one who prays must say the words with his lips. 'And her voice was not heard' — from here, it is forbidden to raise one's voice in his prayer. 'And עלי thought she was drunk' — from here, a drunk person is forbidden to pray.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא goes through one פסוק about חנה, phrase by phrase, and pulls a הלכה out of each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק teaches something different. Heart: כוונה is needed. Lips: thinking alone is not enough, the words must be said. Quiet voice: the עמידה is not said out loud. עלי's suspicion: he scolded her because a drunk person may not pray.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'cut with his lips': say the words clearly

phrases.english: רב המנונא said
How many great הלכות
can be learned
from these פסוקים of חנה
"And חנה spoke in her heart"
From here we learn that one who prays
must focus his heart
"Only her lips moved"
From here, one who prays must form the words with his lips
"And her voice was not heard"
From here, it is forbidden to raise one's voice in his prayer
"And עלי thought she was drunk"
From here, a drunk person is forbidden to pray

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: כַּמָּה הִלְכְתָא גִּבָּרָווֹתָא אִיכָּא לְמִשְׁמַע מֵהָנֵי קְרָאֵי דְחַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to חנה, mentioned in step 32, and learns several more הלכות from her prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prays must have כוונה, say the words with his lips, not raise his voice, and must not pray while drunk.
steps.whatToRemember: From חנה: heart focused, lips moving, voice quiet, and not drunk.
steps.whyThisMatters: These four rules are the basis for how the עמידה is said today: quietly, with the lips, and with כוונה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר starts a lesson from עלי's rebuke of חנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes עלי's words to חנה, 'How long will you be drunk?', and רבי אלעזר begins to learn a lesson about someone who sees something wrong in his friend. The statement continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And עלי said to her: How long will you be drunk…' רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that one who sees in his friend…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new teaching from the next פסוק about עלי and חנה. רבי אלעזר's lesson is only beginning here and finishes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned from what חנה did. Now the focus moves to what עלי did: he spoke up when he thought something was wrong. רבי אלעזר is about to teach what a person should do when he sees something improper in someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the rest of the פסוק)
One who sees something in his friend

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. רבי אלעזר's full lesson continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: "And עלי said to her
How long will you be drunk, etc."
רבי אלעזר said
From here, one who sees in his friend…

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלֶיהָ עֵלִי עַד מָתַי תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִין וְגוֹ׳״. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from עלי's thought (step 36) to his actual words to חנה, and opens a new lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated; רבי אלעזר begins a lesson about one who sees something improper in his friend.
